fieldValues.title: Mined problems enter the corpus as draft suggestions derived from their source, never directly
fieldValues.decision_question: How does a problem statement mined by a model from a transcript or other outside material become a `problem` record in muSrs?
fieldValues.context: The owner, 2026-11-03 (vignette f8e1b034): transcripts are to be mined for problems. The practice already ruled for the owner's own words is that they are recorded verbatim as a Tier-0 vignette and records are derived from them as suggestions with derived-from (clerk handbook, Narrative explorations; decision 77e04b19). The affirmation layer is separate (handbook, The affirmation layer). On 2026-11-03 the local-lab pipeline produced 11 judged-new filing-quality problems from one transcript.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: (a) File nothing automatically and leave mined problems in the lab's results: the 11 good ones are lost to the corpus. (b) File on the judge's score alone, active: a model's judgement enters the corpus with no human act and no provenance. (c) File as draft suggestions through the srs CLI or MCP, with the transcript as a `source` record (private raw text held outside the repository), a derived-from edge to it, a verbatim quote as evidence, and a topic parent; affirmation happens in its own layer.
fieldValues.key_requirements: The write goes through the CLI or MCP so the type and relation contracts hold; the quote is verbatim in the source; the novelty check is against the existing problems; the record is draft until affirmed.
fieldValues.decision_statement: A mined problem enters muSrs only as a draft `problem` record written through the srs CLI or MCP, derived-from a `source` record for the material it came from, carrying its verbatim quote, under a topic parent, in the Problems container. Affirmation is the owner's act in the affirmation layer, never the pipeline's.
fieldValues.rationale: It is the vignette rule applied to a transcript instead of a chat: the words come first as a source, the records are derived suggestions, and the human act of affirming them is kept separate from the machine act of proposing them.
fieldValues.revisit_when: More than a few judged-new suggestions in a run turn out on review to be duplicates, which would mean the novelty check needs an embedding rather than word overlap; or the affirmation editor lands and suggestions can be reviewed there instead of in a PR.
fieldValues.next_steps: File the 11 problems from the 3Nov transcript (P-122 to P-132) as draft suggestions in a PR labelled gate:owner-merge; record the source as a `source` record of kind transcript.
